extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers in mathematical logic (readers of 'A Mathematical Introduction to Logic')
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and constructive results for when functions, relations, and syntactic operations (via Gödel numbering and sequence encodings) are representable in the theory Cn AE (i.e., in first-order arithmetic). Includes closure properties, encodings, and key theorems used in arithmetization of syntax and incompleteness proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: μ-operator (least-zero) representability
rubrics_metrics.description: If a (m+1)-place function g is representable and for every a1,...,am there is a b such that g(a1,...,am,b)=0, then the m-place function f defined by f(a1,...,am) = the least b such that g(a1,...,am,b)=0 (written μb[g(...)=0]) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The representating formula for the graph of f is obtained by formalizing: ψ(v1,v2,0) ∧ ∀y(y < v2 → ¬ψ(v1,y,0)). This is often called the μ-operator (least-zero operator). Theorem 33N formalizes this and the proof reduces the claim to representability of the underlying relation R and use of the least-zero construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantifier-free definability implies representability; closure under boolean operations and bounded quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: As a consequence of Theorem 33I, any relation with a quantifier-free definition in N is representable in Cn AE. The class of representable relations is closed under unions, intersections, and complements, and if R is representable then relations defined by bounded universal/existential conditions over R (e.g., for all c < b, ...) are also representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supplies a baseline 'language' L for building definable/representable relations: atomic formulas, sentential connectives, and bounded quantifiers may be used to guarantee representability. Unbounded quantifiers are not in general allowed for immediate representability without further work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability equivalence with characteristic function
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation R is representable iff its characteristic function K_R is representable (K_R(a)=1 when a∈R, =0 otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a formula representing K_R one can easily obtain a formula representing R (e.g., ψ(v1,S0) represents R). Conversely, from a formula representing R one can form a formula representing K_R by case distinction: (ϕ(v1) ∧ v2 = S0) ∨ (¬ϕ(v1) ∧ v2 = 0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure under composition with representable functions (substitution)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a representable m-ary relation and f1,...,fm are representable functions, then the relation {a | R(f1(a),...,fm(a))} is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows because the characteristic function at a is obtained by composing K_R with the representable functions f1,...,fm. The text gives examples of rearranging and repeating variables to produce representable relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure under bounded 'exists ≤ b' and 'forall ≤ b' projections
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is representable (of arity m+1) then the relations {(a1,...,am,b) | for some c ≤ b, (a1,...,am,c) ∈ R} and {(a1,...,am,b) | for all c ≤ b, (a1,...,am,c) ∈ R} are representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalog items demonstrate construction of such 'prefix' and 'bounded quantifier' relations from R by shifting and applying earlier closure properties (e.g., using successor S to reduce the ≤ case to the < case already handled).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisibility is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The binary relation 'a divides b in N' is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because a divides b iff there exists q ≤ b with a·q = b, and the multiplication relation is quantifier-free definable, the divisibility relation is obtained by applying the bounded-exists construction to the quantifier-free definable relation {(a,b,q) | a·q=b}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primality and adjacent primes are representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of primes and the set of pairs of adjacent primes are representable relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjacency can be defined by: a and b are prime, a<b, and there is no prime c with a<c<b. Each clause can be formalized by numeralwise determined formulas, making the relations representable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime-listing function pa is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The function pa whose value at a is p_a (the (a+1)-th prime) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives a representable characterization using an auxiliary number c that encodes prime exponents satisfying (i)–(iii). A constructive witness c (product of primes to powers) is provided when pa=b, and conversely the conditions on c force b to be the (a+1)-st prime. This function is then used to encode finite sequences via prime-power encodings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence encoding (prime-power coding) is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: For each m, the function that maps (a0,...,am) to the single number coded as ∏_{i≤m} p_{a_i+1}^{i} (i.e., (a0,...,am)) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encoding (and its variants) is used to pack finite sequences into single natural numbers; it relies on the representability of the prime-listing function and prime-power arithmetic. Alternative pairing/concatenation encodings are discussed (e.g., polynomial-rate pairing J(a,b) or base-concatenation in base 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decoding function (sequence projection) is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable function whose value at (a,b) (where a is a sequence-number encoding a0,...,am) is (a)_b = a_b (the b-th component of the encoded sequence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define (a)_b as the least n such that either a=0 or p_{n+2}^b does not divide a; then (a)_b equals the appropriate exponent minus 1 (not less than 0). Use the least-zero operator / μ-operator to show representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability of the set of sequence numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: A number b is a sequence number iff for some m≥-1 and some a0,...,am we have b = (a0,...,am). The set of sequence numbers is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the representability of the coding function and its properties (exercise referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length function lh is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable function lh such that lh((a0,...,am)) = m+1 (the length of the sequence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define lh(a) as the least n such that either a=0 or p_n does not divide a; then apply the μ-operator representability result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction (prefix) of sequence is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable function (a)▯b (restriction of a to b) such that for b ≤ m+1, (a0,...,am) ▯ b = (a0,...,a_{b-1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the restriction as the least n meeting certain divisibility conditions ensuring n encodes the prefix; use the μ-operator to show representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive recursion preserves representability (construction f from g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a (k+2)-place representable function g, there is a unique (k+1)-place function f satisfying f(a,b) = g(f(a,b), a, b) (encoding of initial segment values); if g is representable then f is representable (Theorem 33P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct f(a,b) as the least s that is a sequence number of length a and whose i-th component equals g(s▯i, i, b) for all i<a; then apply μ-operator and earlier closure properties. This formalizes primitive-recursive constructions and enables formalizing common recursion schemas (also used to justify Exercise 8-type constructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounded product/sum over i<a of a representable function is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: For a representable function F, functions G(a,b) = ∏_{i<a} F(i,b) and similarly sums are representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define G recursively: G(0,b)=1; G(a+1,b)=F(a,b)·G(a,b), then apply primitive recursion representability (Exercise 8 method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concatenation of sequence numbers is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: Define concatenation a * b so that (a1,...,am) * (b1,...,bn) = (a1,...,am,b1,...,bn); this concatenation is a representable function and associative on sequence numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit multiplicative formula using prime powers is given; representability follows from closure properties and representability of basic arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterated concatenation (capital-asterisk) is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: For a representable F, the function ∗_{i<a} F(i,b) = F(0,b) * F(1,b) * ... * F(a-1,b) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recursion: base is empty sequence 1; iterate concatenation using previous item and primitive recursion closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Godel-numbering of expressions and sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign to each symbol s an integer h(s) (even/odd coding as described); for an expression ε = s0...sn define its Gödel number ⌜ε⌝ as the sequence number (h(s0),...,h(sn)). To a sequence of expressions assign G(α0,...,αn)=⌜⌜α0⌝,...,⌜αn⌝⌝. Various relations/functions about these Gödel numbers will be representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter fixes a particular scheme (Table IX) but allows any recursively numbered language with 0 and S, with the mild representability condition on the sets of predicate/function symbol codes. Subsequent items formalize representability of syntactic notions via these Gödel numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Godel-numbered syntactic classes are representable: variables, terms, atomic formulas, wffs, sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: The sets of Gödel numbers of variables; of terms; of atomic formulas; of well-formed formulas (wffs); and of sentences (closed formulas) are all representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each class is defined inductively in terms of smaller Gödel numbers; representability is shown by defining the characteristic function via primitive recursion with suitable finite bounds (e.g., i < a^{a^{lh a}} used as a bound) and reducing membership tests to representable/quantifier-bounded relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution function Sb (syntactic substitution) is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable function Sb such that Sb(⌜α⌝, ⌜x⌝, ⌜t⌝) = ⌜α[x:=t]⌝ (the Gödel number of the result of substituting term t for variable x in α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sb is defined by six syntactic clauses (variables, function/predicate application, negation, implication, quantifier cases, and default), and obtained by primitive recursion G(Sb(a,b,c),a,b,c). The graph is a union of six representable relations corresponding to the clauses; careful uniqueness ensures G is a function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gödel-numbered successor-term function is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The function whose value at n is ⌜S^n 0⌝ (the Gödel number of n as a term) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define recursively f(0)=⌜0⌝, f(n+1)=⌜S⌝ * f(n) and apply representability under recursion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free occurrence relation Fr is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable relation Fr such that (⌜α⌝,⌜x⌝) ∈ Fr iff the variable x occurs free in α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use substitution: x occurs free in α iff substituting 0 for x changes α, formalized as Sb(⌜α⌝,⌜x⌝,⌜0⌝) ≠ ⌜α⌝; this condition is representable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitutability relation Sbl is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a representable relation Sbl such that (⌜α⌝,⌜x⌝,⌜t⌝) ∈ Sbl iff t is substitutable for x in α (no variable-capture problems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text states this as item 9 and leaves a proof as an exercise; the representability follows by analyzing free occurrences and bound-variable structure via Gödel-number manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization relation Gen is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The relation Gen where (a,b) ∈ Gen iff a is the Gödel number of a formula and b is the Gödel number of a generalization of that formula (adding universal quantifiers) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define recursively: a=b or b = ⌜∀⌝ * i * j where i codes a variable and (a,j)∈Gen. Use characteristic-function recursion arguments to show representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautology/test-of-validity machinery is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of tautologies is representable. The construction uses: (11.1) representability of the relation listing prime constituents of a formula; (11.2) a representable function P listing the Gödel numbers of prime constituents; (11.3) representable condition for an integer v to encode a truth assignment for α; and (11.4) a representable relation Tr such that (⌜α⌝, v) ∈ Tr iff the truth assignment encoded by v satisfies α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By bounding the quantification over truth assignments (using representable upper bounds derived from P(⌜α⌝)), one can express 'α is a tautology' as a bounded universal condition over v and thereby obtain representability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability of standard logical axiom-shapes and specific schema instances
rubrics_metrics.description: The sets of Gödel numbers of formulas of the forms used in logical axioms (e.g., ∀x ϕ → ϕ[x:=t], ∀x(α→β)→∀xα→∀xβ, α→∀xα when x not free in α, x=x, and x=y→α→α for partial substitutions) are representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each schema is characterized by bounded existential searches over subformula Gödel numbers and substitutability checks; the partial-substitution relation Psb used in the last case is explicitly constructed and representable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set of logical axioms is representable
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of Gödel numbers of logical axioms (instances of the schema sets in the previous item, including generalizations) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formula is a logical axiom iff it is a generalization of some instance in the finite lists produced in items 11–16; representability follows by combining prior items and bounded quantification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability of deductions from finite axioms (proof enumerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite set A of formulas, the set {G(D) | D is a deduction from A} (Gödel numbers of deductions from A) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: d is the Gödel number of a deduction iff it is a sequence of positive length and each component is either a member of A, a logical axiom, or obtained by modus ponens from earlier components. The conditions are bounded (indices < lh d) and thus representable when ⌜A⌝ is representable (trivial for finite A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence: recursive relations ↔ representable in Cn AE
rubrics_metrics.description: Any recursive relation is representable in Cn AE, and conversely any relation representable in Cn AE is recursive (Theorem 34A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof reduces recursive relations to existence of least deductions from a finite set A of sentences that decide membership; conversely earlier results showed many natural recursive syntactic relations are representable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provability (CnA) is recursively enumerable; definability of consequence from recursive axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: If ⌜A⌝ is recursive then ⌜Cn A⌝ need not be recursive but is recursively enumerable: a ∈ ⌜Cn A⌝ iff ∃d[d is the number of a deduction from A and the last component of d is a and a is the Gödel number of a sentence].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existential quantifier over d yields recursively enumerable (r.e.) characterization because the property 'd is a deduction from A with last component a' is recursive when ⌜A⌝ is recursive (item 18). This is later restated as Theorem 35I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete recursively axiomatizable theories are decidable (representable set of consequences is recursive)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ⌜A⌝ is recursive and Cn A is a complete theory, then ⌜Cn A⌝ is recursive (decidable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct g(s) to be the least deduction witnessing either s or ¬s from A; s ∈ ⌜Cn A⌝ iff the last component of g(s) is s. This parallels earlier corollary that complete axiomatizable theories are decidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-point (diagonal) lemma (existence of self-referential sentences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given any formula β(v1) with only v1 free, one can find a sentence σ such that AE proves σ ↔ β(S(⌜σ⌝)0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a representable θ that maps (⌜α⌝,n) to ⌜α(S^n 0)⌝ (items 5 and 6), then substitutes the Gödel number q of the constructed formula into its free variable to obtain σ. This lemma is pivotal for constructing sentences that 'speak about' their own Gödel numbers and is central to incompleteness arguments.
